To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) calcium binding to the alpha-amylase structures increases the stability of the native structure and (ii) the effect of calcium binding is proportional to the number and strength of the interactions between the protein structure and the bound calcium ions.
The unfolding barrier of homologous alpha- amylases is increased by calcium binding, and the effect is related to the number of Ca2+ ions bound.

the stabilization of alpha-amylases upon calcium binding is due to an enthalpic contribution, that the enthalpy increase is caused by an increase of hydrogen bond interactions between the protein and the calcium ions, and that the enthalpic contribution to the unfolding barrier is compensated by an increase of entropy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of stabilization upon calcium binding and shows that calcium binding to the alpha-amylase structures is a prerequisite for extreme thermostabilities.
the mechanism of protein stabilization by calcium ions and provides evidence that the unfolding barrier height is the major factor in the thermostability of alpha-amylases.
the mechanism of stabilization by calcium binding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium binding to alpha-amylases increases the stability of the native structure by increasing the enthalpic contribution to the unfolding barrier.
the calcium binding to the protein structures leads to a stabilization of the transition state.
calcium binding to the enzyme structure causes an increase in the unfolding barrier by an enthalpy-driven mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium binding to alpha-amylases increases the enthalpy of unfolding, and that the entropic contributions to the unfolding reaction are not altered significantly.
for alpha-amylases the binding of calcium ions to the protein structures is a key mechanism to achieve extreme thermal stabilities.
the unfolding barriers of alpha-amylases are determined by the calcium binding properties of the proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stabilization of the transition state by calcium ions is a major contribution to the stabilization of these alpha-amylases.
calcium ions can be considered as a general protein stabilizer.
the stabilization effect of calcium binding is not due to the entropic contribution but rather to the enthalpic contribution.
